neighbours.label: Taking the wide view rather than the close one: zooming out, the bigger picture, a sweeping scope or scale
fire: When you zoom out on the chart, the long-term trend appears.
The film unfolds on a vast scale, following armies across a continent.
Her lecture offered a wider perspective on global trade.
The sweeping panorama covers two thousand years of history.
He urged them to step back and see the bigger picture.
Viewed at the macro level, the economy looks healthy.
This survey has a sweeping scope, covering every country in Asia.
The author's broad vision takes in the entire history of science.
quiet: When you zoom in on the chart, the daily noise appears.
The film unfolds in a small room, following two sisters through one evening.
Her lecture offered a close reading of one trade contract.
The narrow study covers two weeks of one village's history.
He urged them to lean in and check the fine print.
Viewed at the street level, the shop looks healthy.
This survey has a limited remit, covering one school in Hanoi.
The author's careful notes take in a single species of moth.

predictions: Zoomed-out wording fires; the zoomed-in counterpart with the same frame stays quiet.
